desk_read: Yesterday's session was characterized by widespread short covering across commodities alongside fresh selling pressure in equities. Crude oil, natural gas, and gold all managed positive price gains while seeing total open interest contract, led by a 2.5 percent drop in WTI total open interest alongside 0.8x average volume and a backwardated curve. Conversely, equity index futures faced heavy downside pressure as S&P 500 prices fell 1.08 percent alongside a 3.0 percent surge in total open interest on 1.0x average volume, indicating aggressive new shorts. Meanwhile, Copper also saw prices decline 0.36 percent alongside falling open interest of 1.6 percent on above-average volume of 1.2x.
oil_read: Yesterday's session showed WTI (CLF27) up +0.21% with total open interest down -31.9k contracts (-2.5%) and volume at 0.8x its 20-day average, indicating short covering in a backwardated curve where the CLZ26-CLK27 spread was +6.31 $/bbl. Brent (BZG27) rose +0.38% with total open interest down -629 contracts (-0.5%) and volume 0.7x its 20-day average, also reflecting short covering in backwardation with the BZF27-BZM27 spread at +9.14 $/bbl, while the Brent-WTI F27 spread stood at +8.80 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a neutral bias driven by short covering with a weakening backwardation curve, while Brent sits at mildly bullish with backwardation steepening on light volume 0.7x the 20-day average, both warning that the current moves lack durable momentum. Silver displays a mildly bullish bias with volume 1.4x the 20-day average, where this conviction supports the trend despite short covering. Meanwhile, Nasdaq 100 features a mildly bearish bias driven by new shorts, where fresh positions warn of downward exhaustion. Overall, the short term flow reveals a fragmented landscape with selective conviction in metals contrasting against fleeting short-covering across energy and equities.
